note: DRAFT SCRIPT, MACHINE-GENERATED. Most of this is combinatorial: a small set of carrier-phrase templates (validated in v1's original 40 prompts) filled in with varying numbers, names, places, items, days, and times, which is a legitimate way to reach broad coverage for those slots but still means the underlying grammar has not been checked by a native Shona speaker. The natural-conversation, confirmation, error, and mixed-terms categories are hand-written, not templated, and carry the same caveat. reports_and_insights is deliberately longer-form (multi-sentence paragraphs, not short carrier phrases) because that's what Smart-Qx's TTS actually reads aloud in production -- narrated sales/stock/cash-flow reports and a grounded coaching insight (see smart-w/utility.py narrate_for_tts and _grounded_sales_insight) -- so this category needs the most scrutiny of all of them: longer text compounds any grammar issue. Sized for roughly 5+ hours of reading material overall so a speaker can keep recording past the 2-hour baseline the app tracks, without running out of prompts. A native Shona speaker should review and prune this before it drives a real session -- treat volume as a ceiling to draw from, not a quota to complete.
